 The Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Aday Mara, and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Pelicans on Friday. 
 It was previously reported that Micah Peavy would be starting in place Aday Mara, but Mara will get the nod. Mara is a streamer and Peavy isn’t anything more than a deeper league guy. 
 -  Brian Taylor 
 Source:  Clemente Almanza

 Aday Mara accounted for 10 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-4 Fts), six rebounds, eight assists and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks. 
 Mara returned to the Thunder starting lineup on Wednesday, replacing Kenrich Williams. The rookie center may not have lit up the scoreboard, but he recorded a season-high eight assists. During his one season at Michigan, Mara was given the freedom to facilitate offense, a skill that should serve him well in the NBA. That ability may help the Thunder relieve some of the pressure on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, as long as Mara is consistently productive. 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander notched 34 points (14-of-29 FGs, 5-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander once again led the way for the Thunder, with Wednesday’s game being his ninth this season with at least 30 points. However, SGA shot a surprising 5-of-10 from the foul line. He’s still making 83.5 percent of his attempts for the season, so the sky certainly isn’t falling. The one concern for Gilgeous-Alexander is whether the heavy lifting he’s being asked to do this early due to injuries will impact his effectiveness later in the season. 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #2 
 The Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Aday Mara, and Isaiah Hartenstein on Wednesday against the Hawks. 
 Aday Mara will start in place of Kenrich Williams on Wednesday. Mara can be used as a streamer if you need the points and rebounds. The Thunder keep tinkering with their starting lineup and will likely continue to do so unless someone establishes themselves. 
 Jaylin Williams 
 OKC 
 Forward 
 #6 
 Jaylin Williams (back) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Williams has missed Oklahoma City’s last seven games, leaving the Thunder to count mainly on Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara in the post. Mara’s minutes could decrease if JayWill returns, but he should still be in the rotation. 
 Aday Mara 
 OKC 
 Center 
 #15 
 Aday Mara tallied 16 points (8-of-11 FGs), 13 rebounds and three assists in Sunday’s win over the Kings. 
 In addition to recording his third double-double, Mara established a new career high with 13 rebounds. While the rookie center didn’t record any defensive stats on Sunday, he’s emerged as a player worth rostering in some 12-team leagues. The only thing working against Mara in the short term is the schedule, as the Thunder won’t play again until Wednesday. 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Sunday’s win over the Kings with 37 points (13-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers. 
 In his final game of Week 4, Gilgeous-Alexander did whatever he wanted against the Kings. While shooting 65 percent from the field, the two-time MVP did not turn the ball over at all in 30 minutes of action. Oklahoma City’s blowout win meant Gilgeous-Alexander got some additional rest, as he did not play in the fourth quarter. SGA and the Thunder don’t play the first of their three Week 5 games until Wednesday. That isn’t great for fantasy managers, but it’s good for a team that’s been hit hard by injuries this season. 
 Kenrich Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #34 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Sunday’s game against the Kings. 
 Mitchell is back in the Thunder lineup after a two-game absence. However, instead of Williams, Aday Mara will head to the bench. The rookie center will remain in the rotation, but his fantasy ceiling takes a hit with the lineup change. 
 Jaylin Williams 
 OKC 
 Forward 
 #6 
 Jaylin Williams (back) has been ruled out against the Kings on Sunday. 
 This will be a seventh straight absence for Williams, with no end in sight. Aday Mara should continue to start alongside Isaiah Hartenstein down low. 
 Aday Mara 
 OKC 
 Center 
 #15 
 Aday Mara recorded 10 points (5-of-6 FGs), three rebounds and three blocks in Friday’s loss to the Clippers. 
 While Mara has started four of Oklahoma City’s last six games, the 21 minutes he logged on Friday were the least he’s played in any of those starts. There were some positives to the rookie’s performance, specifically the field-goal percentage and blocked shots. However, Mara hasn’t done enough with Chet Holmgren (knee) out to become a player who has to be rostered in 12-team leagues. 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.

 Nic Claxton got himself 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, an assist, and two blocks in start on Friday against Wizards. 
 In his first start with the Bulls, Claxton had a fine game but nothing crazy to go crazy about. It took Jalen Smith getting hurt for him to get the start. The hopes of him returning to his play in Brooklyn seem to be fading. For his redraft outlook, he’s a streamer for rebounds, but not a lot of upside. Jalen Smith was out with an illness, so it’s possible that he’s back next game.

 Norman Powell put up 16 points (7-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, a steal, and a three in loss to the Wizards on Friday. 
 Powell took advantage of the Wizards lack of effort on the defensive end. He got going in the first quarter and didn’t look back. He was the reason why the Bulls stayed in the game in the first half before the bench got into the game. On the season, he’s been marginally disappointing with his efficiency, but his counting stats have been close to what they were last season.

 AJ Dybantsa had himself a night with 20 points (9-of-18 FGs), ten rebounds, six assists, two steals, a block, and two 3-pointers in win over the Bulls on Friday. 
 Coming off his first career double-double, Dybantsa was one of the few players giving consistent effort on the defensive end in the first half. He crashed the glass and passed the ball well. While the Wizards have had defensive issues, he’s not the reason for it which has been great to see given the concerns coming out of college. There is a sell high window here if you can manage it, but if you can’t manage it, enjoy the production.

 Anthony Davis had a monster 36 points (16-of-26 FGs, 4-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds, and three assists in the 98-94 win to the Bulls on Friday. 
 The Wizards really needed his offense, especially in the first half. Without him, the Wizards would’ve been down by way more in the first half which could’ve led to another loss. Davis has been the best player on the Wizards this season and he has done a good job rehabilitating his value. As long as he’s healthy, the fantasy numbers will be there.

 Jalen Johnson led the Hawks with 26 points (10-of-15 FGs), six rebounds, six assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in a 111-97 win over the Hornets on Friday.
 Johnson’s early-season shooting percentages have been incredibly rough, so this was an encouraging performance. He is still stuffing the stat sheet, but he needs to shoot much better to live up to his ADP. Johnson’s production dropped late last season after the Hawks acquired CJ McCollum, so with both McCollum and Kingston Flemings out, the ball will be in Johnson’s hands even more. Hopefully he can take advantage of the opportunity and start having more performances like this one.
 -  Noah Rubin

 James Harden 
 CLE 
 Guard 
 #1

 James Harden erupted for 51 points (15-of-26 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), six rebounds, six assists and one steal over 40 minutes to lead the Cavaliers to a 128-119 win over the Pacers on Friday.
 Harden reached the 50-point plateau for the 26th time in his career, accomplishing the feat for the first time in a Cavaliers uniform after sinking a pair of free throws in the final minute. His seven three-pointers and 14 free throw attempts were both season highs. The 37-year-old veteran wasted little time finding his rhythm, pouring in 24 first-half points on an efficient 8-of-14 shooting, including 3-of-6 from beyond the arc, while adding five assists. He was Cleveland’s lone starter to reach double figures before halftime and continued to pile on after the break, surpassing 40 points with just over a minute remaining in the third quarter. After a sluggish start to the season, Harden has shown encouraging signs of life as a scoring threat over the past couple of weeks. The Cavaliers return to action for a three-game week featuring matchups against the Bulls, Knicks and Heat.
 -  George Bissell

 Ivica Zubac posted a double-double with 21 points (8-of-11 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, two assists and three blocks over 27 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
 Zubac notched a double-double for the fourth time in eight games since returning from an ankle injury earlier this month. This was just the fourth time this season that he attempted 10 shots or more. Simply put, the Pacers are an entirely different team without facilitating superstar Tyrese Haliburton, who remains out with a left hamstring injury. Indiana closes out the week with a road tilt against the Knicks on Sunday.
 -  George Bissell

 Peyton Watson tallied 15 points (6-of-9 FGs), four rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block over 29 minutes in Friday’s win over the Pacers.
 Watson delivered one of his strongest performances of the season in his return to Cleveland’s lineup after sustaining a back contusion during a midair collision with Bulls center Jalen Smith earlier this week. He managed just seven points in a relatively quiet first half before opening the third quarter with back-to-back three-pointers, helping spark a 43-22 Cavaliers run that effectively swung the game in Cleveland’s favor. The 24-year-old hasn’t exactly made an offensive leap in his Cavaliers debut, but he’s in an ideal situation to thrive given the surrounding talent.
 -  George Bissell

 Pascal Siakam 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #43 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Pascal Siakam posted 21 points (8-of-17 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 30 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
 Siakam did most of his damage in the second half, but it simply wasn’t enough for Indiana to overcome a monster 50-point effort from James Harden on a night where Cleveland knocked down a staggering 19-of-44 (43 percent) from three-point range. The 32-year-old veteran forward remains a bankable scoring threat for fantasy managers, supplying at least 20 points in 12 of 15 games this season, but he doesn’t offer much in the remaining categories besides chipping in a handful of rebounds. Things have looked very similar to last year for Indiana over the last few weeks while Tyrese Haliburton remains sidelined with a left hamstring strain. The Pacers close out the week with a road matchup against the Knicks on Sunday.
 -  George Bissell
